image_description: A close-up photograph of a brown butterfly, identified as a Ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), perched on green vegetation. The wings are held closed, displaying the ventral side which is light brown with distinct rows of black eyespots (ocelli) ringed in yellow/white. The body is fuzzy and dark brown. The background consists of out-of-focus green grass blades.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left antenna is clearly visible extending from the head; it shows the characteristic thickening at the tip (club) typical of butterflies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Satyrid butterfly with moderately sized wingspan.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject matches the general morphology of a Satyrid. While absolute size is hard to judge without a scale, the proportions relative to the grass blade are consistent with a small-to-medium butterfly (30-50mm).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings uniformly brown to dark brown with small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible wing surface is brown/tan. There are multiple distinct eyespots: two large ones on the hindwing and one smaller one on the forewing, arranged in a linear pattern consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings held closed at rest revealing cryptic ventral patterning.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The butterfly is viewed from the side with wings pressed together, showing the underside (ventral) pattern which serves as camouflage against the green/brown background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brown body integument matching wing coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The thorax and abdomen are covered in dark brown hairs that blend well with the darker tones of the wing base.
The thorax appears robust and densely pilose (hairy), while the abdomen tapers, fitting the 'slender hairy' description for this family.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Reduced brush-like forelegs characteristic of nymphalids.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While Ringlets are Nymphalids and possess reduced forelegs, they are tucked against the head/thorax and are not resolvable in this specific image angle/resolution. Marking untestable to avoid hallucination.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (three tagmata).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The division between head, thorax, and abdomen is visually apparent, consistent with insect anatomy.
